description: C++ programs for the ESP32 development board.

lessons.name: 01 Blink LED
lessons.description: Blink an LED using the ESP32.
lessons.connectionGuide:
ESP32:
Use GPIO 2 for the LED.

External LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> GPIO 2
Cathode (-) -> GND

Many ESP32 DevKit boards also have a built-in LED on GPIO 2.

lessons.name: 02 Button Input
lessons.description: Read a push button and control an LED.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Push Button:
One leg -> ESP32 GPIO 4
Other leg -> GND

LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> GPIO 2
Cathode (-) -> GND

The internal pull-up resistor is enabled.

lessons.name: 03 Buzzer
lessons.description: Generate a tone using a buzzer.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Buzzer:
Positive (+) -> ESP32 GPIO 25
Negative (-) -> GND

This example uses the ESP32 LEDC tone function.

lessons.name: 04 Traffic Light
lessons.description: Control red, yellow, and green LEDs using the ESP32.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Red LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> GPIO 25
Cathode (-) -> GND

Yellow LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> GPIO 26
Cathode (-) -> GND

Green LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> GPIO 27
Cathode (-) -> GND.

lessons.name: 05 Serial Monitor
lessons.description: Display messages and sensor values in the Serial Monitor.
lessons.connectionGuide:
No external components are required.

Connect the ESP32 to the computer using USB.

Open Arduino IDE -> Tools -> Serial Monitor.
Set the baud rate to 115200.

GPIO 34 is input-only and is used here for analog reading.

lessons.name: 06 Analog Input
lessons.description: Read an analog value from a potentiometer.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Potentiometer:
One outer pin -> 3.3V
Middle pin -> GPIO 34
Other outer pin -> GND

ESP32 ADC readings are typically from 0 to 4095.

lessons.name: 07 LED Fade
lessons.description: Fade an LED using ESP32 PWM.
lessons.connectionGuide:
LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> GPIO 18
Cathode (-) -> GND

GPIO 18 is used for PWM control.

lessons.name: 08 Light Sensor
lessons.description: Read an LDR and automatically control an LED.
lessons.connectionGuide:
LDR circuit:
Use the LDR and a 10K resistor as a voltage divider.

Voltage divider output -> GPIO 34

LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> GPIO 2
Cathode (-) -> GND

The LED turns ON when the measured value is below 2000.

lessons.name: 09 Button Counter
lessons.description: Count button presses and display the count in Serial Monitor.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Push Button:
One leg -> ESP32 GPIO 4
Other leg -> GND

The internal pull-up resistor is used.

Open Serial Monitor at 115200 baud.

lessons.name: 10 Button LED Toggle
lessons.description: Toggle an LED ON and OFF each time the button is pressed.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Push Button:
One leg -> ESP32 GPIO 4
Other leg -> GND

LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> GPIO 2
Cathode (-) -> GND

Each button press toggles the LED between ON and OFF.
